cells.tense: You are keeping the scale level right now, in the room where something is growing.
cells.ask: Say the rule you're applying with the young one, once, before you enforce it.
cells.core: You know what's fair in this house, not as a rule you recite — as a thing you feel in your chest. You can tell when a share is off, when someone got more than they were owed, when you got exactly what you gave. That sense has been sitting next to you while you tend what's growing here, and it's been steady. It doesn't need arguing and it doesn't need proof.\n\nWhat it buys you is a house where the scales stay even with people only half grown. Fairness isn't applied to them from above. It lives down where they are. You can keep doing that — know the standard, name it now and then, don't let it harden into a rule nobody remembers agreeing to. That's the whole of it.
cells.sheetLine: You keep the scales even where something is only half grown.
cells.verb: weighing what's fair before it's handed down
cells.place: at the table where something is being raised

cells.tense: You are already auditing a share that hasn't been handed out yet.
cells.ask: Take one thing you're measuring against someone not yet in the room and set it down for today.
cells.core: You can feel the unfairness coming. Before anyone has taken a share, before the thing you're raising has even grown into its claim, you know what it'll owe and what it won't get. You're running the account ahead of the moment, and it looks like care because it is care. But the care has gone past tending and started supervising.\n\nThe scale you trust is real, and using it this way presses it flat. You're forcing fairness to arrive before the thing is grown enough to receive it. The proportion you're protecting becomes something you impose. Hold the scale open a little — let one share go unweighed until it's actually asked for. The fairness you're guarding lives on the other side of that waiting.

cells.tense: You know what fairness is here and you've stopped saying it out loud.
cells.ask: Tell one person tending something beside you about an exchange here that struck you as off.
cells.core: There's a scale in you and you stopped reading it here. You kept the sense and dropped the act of handing it down. Now the thing you're raising grows without the scale beside it, and what you feel about balance doesn't leave your body.\n\nWhat's missing is the gesture — the moment of naming a share as unfair before the young one has to guess it. It doesn't have to be proof or a whole lecture. One sentence, said at the table, while the thing is still small enough to hear it. That is what recharges the room, not more feeling pushed from behind.

cells.tense: You are running the scale right now and telling anyone it is just what seems normal.
cells.ask: Name one balance you keep in this house and call it yours, out loud, once.
cells.core: Something in this room stays even and you're the one keeping it. You decide what gets shared out, who waits, whose turn gets skipped — and you do it in a way people can feel. None of that is luck. You feel the weight of it when the call comes.\n\nBut you talk about the evenness like it lives in the room by itself. You call it just how things are, just being fair, as if the scale were part of the furniture. The weighing is happening. The saying 'I'm the one holding this' isn't. One small admission would change what you can do here — and you can make it without a whole accounting.
cells.sheetLine: You keep the scales even and call it just how things are.

attempts.check: The record describes the inner moral compass and its seat in nurturing; it does not establish that the person has ever been on the losing end of a fairness account or that someone once overruled them about what was fair, so Too Little must locate the withdrawal from handing down fairness without inventing what was weighed, who judged, or what it cost. The likely objection is 'I never felt owed anything' — the cell answers that the scale itself was not built, not that a debt was suffered. The ask survives being wrong because it is one instruction about something they are raising, made or growing, and it works whether or not the hidden accounting is running. The sentence serving the writer is 'the knowing never left' — a line that comforts the card's story more than the person; it is cut.
